top.title: Snowflake Marketplace Partners Earn $100M in the First Half of 2026
top.summary: Snowflake Marketplace partners achieved $100M+ revenue in H1 2026, representing 277% year-over-year growth, driven by AI agents, Native Apps, and AI-ready data products. Ecosystem expansion demonstrates increasing demand for governed data and AI capabilities.
top.relevance: Signals the platform economics shift toward AI-native architectures and the emergence of data monetization and AI-ready product categories.

top.title: BCG AI Radar 2026: As AI Investments Surge, CEOs Take the Lead
top.summary: Global survey of 2,360 executives reveals corporations expect to double AI spending from 0.8% to 1.7% of revenues in 2026. Nearly three-quarters of CEOs are chief decision makers on AI; CEOs spending 8+ hours weekly on AI capabilities are more likely to generate meaningful value.
top.relevance: Demonstrates CEO-level commitment and investment acceleration across enterprises, establishing the business case and governance context for analytics/AI transformations.

top.title: Powering the Agentic Enterprise: Turning Enterprise Context into Governed Agentic Action
top.summary: Snowflake and Accenture outline the role of governed data and Context Graph in enabling enterprise-scale agentic decision-making. Emphasis on data as prerequisite for reliable AI agent workflows and organizational trust.
top.relevance: Illustrates how leading platform and consulting firms are positioning data governance as the enabling architecture for agentic transformation.

top.title: Four Ways to Accelerate Growth with AI and Analytics
top.summary: BCG outlines strategic use of AI and analytics for competitive advantage: mapping patent networks, mining scientific literature, using agentic AI for real-time anomaly detection, and leveraging customer data at scale. Companies not using analytics to shape growth strategy face significant competitive risk.
top.relevance: Concrete framework for transforming analytics from operational to strategic—essential for leading business-building conversations with C-suite clients.

top.title: Scaling agentic AI with data transformations
top.summary: McKinsey research finds that while two-thirds of enterprises have experimented with agents, fewer than 10% have scaled them; eight in ten cite data limitations as the primary roadblock. Strong data foundations and governed architectures are the critical difference between value creators and non-performers.
top.relevance: Directly addresses the data infrastructure challenge that determines success or failure in scaling agentic AI—a critical operational priority for executives.

top.title: AI Will Reshape More Jobs Than It Replaces
top.summary: BCG analysis of 165 million US jobs across 1,500 roles shows task automation does not equal job loss; most roles will change substantially rather than disappear. Software engineering and advisory roles emerge as 'amplified' (demand increases despite automation).
top.relevance: Essential for consulting strategy—guides change management and talent planning discussions with clients undergoing AI-driven transformations.

top.title: The $200 Billion Agentic AI Opportunity for Tech Service Providers
top.summary: BCG quantifies 0.5-1 percentage point uplift to global IT spending from agentic AI adoption. More than 40% of large enterprises are scaling agentic implementation; 75% want to work with service providers to build or implement priority use cases.
top.relevance: Critical for consulting leaders—identifies the size of agentic AI services opportunity and enterprise demand patterns reshaping consulting delivery models.

top.title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
top.summary: Global survey of 1,993 participants from 105 nations reveals that AI high performers treat AI as organizational catalyst, redesigning workflows and investing heavily in AI capabilities. Data quality, governance, and senior leadership ownership are critical success factors.
top.relevance: Essential baseline research showing how leaders differ in capturing AI value and the governance structures required for enterprise-scale deployment.

top.title: Scaling agentic AI with data transformations
top.summary: McKinsey research on gen AI reshaping data strategy: by 2026, three-quarters of businesses will use gen AI to create synthetic customer data. Successful data monetization strategies start with understanding proprietary advantage; raw data becomes commodity while insights and analytics commands premium.
top.relevance: Reframes data strategy from ownership to advantage—guides executives on shifting from data brokerage to higher-value analytics and AI-driven offerings.

top.title: Charting a path to the data- and AI-driven enterprise of 2030
top.summary: McKinsey roadmap for 2030 enterprise: data ubiquity embedded across systems and decisions with automated actions and human oversight. Talent profiles will shift dramatically as gen AI handles basic tasks; new roles in data engineering, DataOps, and vector database development emerge.
top.relevance: Provides multi-year planning framework for talent, technology, and organizational design—essential for consulting strategy and long-term client roadmaps.

ai.title: Achieving operational excellence with AI
ai.summary: Article explores how AI modernizes operational frameworks that balance statistical rigor and process mapping, shifting from legacy methodologies like Lean Six Sigma to AI-driven automation of operational control loops.
ai.relevance: Offers insights on how analytics and data leaders should rethink operational workflows and governance to leverage agentic AI for sustained competitive advantage in execution and continuous improvement.

ai.title: Teaching AI to run with the turbines
ai.summary: Demonstrates practical agentic AI deployment in industrial operations where AI monitors performance, troubleshoots autonomously, and optimizes solutions in real-time physical infrastructure environments.
ai.relevance: Shows emerging use cases for agentic AI in capital-intensive operations where continuous autonomous monitoring and decision-making create measurable ROI—a key pattern for enterprise AI strategy.

ai.title: LLMs are stuck in a groupthink groove. This startup is trying to get them out.
ai.summary: Identifies a systematic limitation in language models where frontier models exhibit convergent behavior (groupthink) rather than diverse reasoning, with emerging solutions to increase output diversity and reasoning robustness.
ai.relevance: Essential for data leaders evaluating model selection and deployment: highlights a fundamental frontier model limitation that affects reliability of agentic systems and autonomous decision-making at scale.

ai.title: Claude Science is Anthropic's newest flagship product
ai.summary: Anthropic announced Claude Science, a new product designed to support scientific research with autonomous capabilities similar to Claude Code for software engineering. The tool integrates research databases and can execute complex scientific workflows independently.
ai.relevance: Demonstrates frontier model application beyond general enterprise use, showing specialized agentic capabilities for knowledge-intensive domains that drive competitive advantage in analytics and research.

ai.title: Samsung Electronics brings ChatGPT and Codex to employees
ai.summary: Samsung Electronics scaled ChatGPT Enterprise and Codex deployment to employees worldwide, representing one of OpenAI's largest enterprise AI rollouts and demonstrating successful organizational scaling.
ai.relevance: Provides concrete enterprise adoption precedent showing how to operationalize frontier models at scale—critical reference for enterprise leaders planning parallel deployments across global workforces.

ai.title: Introducing the OpenAI Partner Network
ai.summary: OpenAI launches Partner Network with $150M investment to help global partners accelerate enterprise AI adoption, deployment, and transformation through structured consulting and implementation support.
ai.relevance: Important for consulting leaders evaluating partnership models and market positioning: shows how frontier model vendors are shifting toward ecosystem enablement and managed deployment services.

ai.title: Enterprise AI adoption in 2026: Why 79% face challenges despite high investment
ai.summary: WRITER's 2026 survey of 1,200 employees and executives reveals 97% deployed AI agents in the past year, yet 79% face adoption challenges and 54% report AI adoption is tearing companies apart, exposing organizational transformation gaps.
ai.relevance: Critical reality check on enterprise adoption: shows massive deployment velocity coupled with failure to extract business value or align organizational structures—key risk assessment for senior leaders planning agentic AI strategy.

ai.title: Reimagining tech infrastructure for agentic AI
ai.summary: McKinsey examines how agentic AI requires infrastructure transformation, with high performers committing 20%+ of digital budgets to AI, while infrastructure costs are projected to increase 2-3x by 2030.
ai.relevance: Essential for technology and finance leaders planning multi-year infrastructure investments: quantifies the infrastructure cost-benefit tradeoff and shows how agentic AI enables cost containment through autonomous operations management.

ai.title: Scaling agentic AI with data transformations
ai.summary: McKinsey research shows eight in ten companies cite data limitations as roadblocks to scaling agentic AI, requiring federated governance models, continuous quality management, and infrastructure transformation.
ai.relevance: Directly addresses the data & analytics leader's core challenge: without robust data foundations, governance, and infrastructure, agentic AI cannot deliver value—this is the prerequisite roadmap for strategic planning.

ai.title: State of AI trust in 2026: Shifting to the agentic era
ai.summary: McKinsey's 2026 AI Trust Maturity Survey reveals that while trust maturity improved to 2.3 from 2.0, only one-third of organizations reach maturity level three or higher in governance and agentic AI controls, exposing critical governance gaps.
ai.relevance: Critical for planning leaders to understand that agentic AI adoption faces persistent governance and risk management challenges—directly impacting enterprise implementation roadmaps and requiring foundational governance investment.

platforms.title: Databricks Eyes $175B Valuation as IPO Plans Shift to 2027
platforms.summary: Sacra estimates Databricks reached approximately $6.9 billion in annualized revenue in June 2026, growing roughly 80% year-over-year, and is in talks to raise a new funding round at a $165 to $175 billion valuation with Andreessen Horowitz, NEA, and Battery among investors. CEO Ali Ghodsi has signaled the company will not go public in 2026 despite being IPO-ready, pointing toward a possible listing in 2027.
platforms.relevance: The valuation trajectory and IPO timing signal Databricks remains the dominant private enterprise data platform, with implications for competitive positioning, client negotiating leverage, and partnership strategy across the consulting ecosystem.

platforms.title: Announcing Claude Sonnet 5 on Snowflake Cortex AI
platforms.summary: Claude Sonnet 5 is now available in private preview on Snowflake Cortex AI, bringing Anthropic's latest advanced reasoning and agentic capabilities into Snowflake's governed AI platform. This follows Snowflake's multi-year $200 million Anthropic partnership and expands the model roster available natively within Cortex alongside OpenAI and Google Cloud models.
platforms.relevance: The rapid addition of frontier models like Claude Sonnet 5 inside a governed data platform reduces the integration complexity for enterprise AI agents, a key enabler for clients looking to operationalize agentic workflows on existing data estates.

platforms.title: Snowflake Marketplace Partners Earn $100M in the First Half of 2026
platforms.summary: Snowflake Marketplace partners collectively surpassed $100 million in revenue in the first half of 2026, representing 277% year-over-year growth, driven by expanding offerings in AI agents, Snowflake Native Apps, and AI-ready data products. The milestone signals rapid ecosystem monetization and growing partner demand for agentic AI distribution channels on the platform.
platforms.relevance: The 277% ecosystem revenue growth rate is a leading indicator of the commercial viability of building AI-native data products on Snowflake, directly relevant to consulting leaders advising clients on data monetization and ISV partnership strategies.

platforms.title: Snowflake Summit 2026: Context, Custom Model Training, Iceberg V3
platforms.summary: At Summit 2026, Snowflake rebranded Snowflake Intelligence as CoWork and Cortex Code as CoCo, introduced Cortex Sense for grounding AI agents in enterprise metadata, and expanded its AWS partnership while acquiring Natoma. The company also raised its fiscal 2027 growth target to 31%, with analyst commentary highlighting that Snowflake is shifting its competitive focus from data formats to meaning, trust, permissions, and context.
platforms.relevance: Snowflake's pivot toward context and semantic governance as its core differentiator directly shapes how consulting leaders should advise clients on data architecture and AI agent readiness in 2026 and beyond.

platforms.title: Microsoft Build 2026: Building Agentic Apps with Microsoft Fabric and Microsoft Databases
platforms.summary: At Microsoft Build 2026, Microsoft introduced Rayfin, an SDK and CLI making Fabric a production-ready application backend, and Azure HorizonDB, a new PostgreSQL database purpose-built for AI applications now in public preview with vector search and integrated AI model management. Microsoft framed Fabric as the unified data and AI platform that gives AI agents shared organizational context, positioning it as the data backbone of the agentic enterprise.
platforms.relevance: These launches redefine Microsoft Fabric from an analytics platform to a full-stack agentic application substrate, with direct consequences for enterprise architecture decisions and Azure-aligned consulting engagements.

platforms.title: Snowflake Q4 FY 2026 Results Highlight AI-Led Consumption and Platform Expansion
platforms.summary: Futurum Research analysts note that Snowflake exited FY2026 with AI framed as a structural driver of incremental consumption rather than a one-time catalyst, posting a 61% adjusted free cash flow margin while funding acquisitions like Observe. Analysts highlight that management's repositioning of Snowflake from a system enterprises analyze with into one they build on represents the most consequential strategic shift of the year.
platforms.relevance: This third-party analyst take provides consulting leaders with an independent read on the durability of Snowflake's AI consumption model and its expanding competitive surface, critical context for benchmarking platform ROI conversations with clients.

platforms.title: FabCon and SQLCon 2026: Unifying Databases and Fabric on a Single Data Platform
platforms.summary: Microsoft announced that Fabric now serves more than 31,000 customers, just two and a half years after reaching general availability, making it the fastest-growing data platform in Microsoft history. New capabilities include Fabric Runtime 2.0 with Apache Spark 4.x and Delta Lake 4.x, generally available materialized lake views, and a new migration assistant for Azure Data Factory and Synapse Analytics pipelines.
platforms.relevance: With 31,000 customers and accelerating Synapse migration tooling, Fabric adoption is at an inflection point that creates immediate client advisory and implementation opportunities for consulting practices with Azure practices.

platforms.title: Snowflake Reports Financial Results for the Fourth Quarter and Full-Year of Fiscal 2026
platforms.summary: Snowflake reported Q4 FY2026 product revenue of $1.23 billion, up 30% year-over-year, with remaining performance obligations of $9.77 billion growing 42% year-over-year and 430-plus new product capabilities shipped in the fiscal year. Key milestones include the launch of Cortex Code, expanded partnerships with Anthropic, Google Cloud, and OpenAI, and the acquisition of Observe to enter the IT operations market.
platforms.relevance: The combination of accelerating RPO growth, broad product velocity, and entry into the IT observability market signals Snowflake is expanding its total addressable footprint in the enterprise, with implications for how consulting practices size and scope Snowflake-anchored engagements.

platforms.title: Databricks Grows >65% YoY, Surpasses $5.4 Billion Revenue Run-Rate, Doubles Down on Lakebase and Genie
platforms.summary: Databricks reported over 65% year-over-year growth in Q4, crossing a $5.4 billion revenue run-rate, and completed a funding round exceeding $7 billion including approximately $5 billion in equity at a $134 billion valuation. The company is directing capital toward accelerating Lakebase, its serverless Postgres database for AI agents, and Genie, its conversational AI assistant for enterprise data access.
platforms.relevance: The scale and pace of Databricks growth, combined with its dual focus on AI-native databases and conversational data access, directly shapes enterprise platform decisions for clients evaluating data and AI infrastructure investments in 2026.

platforms.title: Snowflake and OpenAI Forge $200 Million Partnership to Bring Enterprise-Ready AI to the World's Most Trusted Data Platform
platforms.summary: Snowflake and OpenAI announced a multi-year, $200 million partnership covering co-innovation and joint go-to-market strategies for AI agents, making OpenAI models natively available to Snowflake's 12,600 global customers within Cortex AI across all three major clouds. The deal enables enterprises to build custom AI agents that reason over governed Snowflake data without moving data outside the platform.
platforms.relevance: This partnership substantially expands the scope of governed agentic AI deployable on Snowflake and raises the stakes for enterprises evaluating multi-model AI strategies, directly informing platform selection and AI governance frameworks in client engagements.

planning.title: Anaplan Introduces Agentic Enterprise with AI-Powered Role-Based Agents and 12 New Purpose-Built Applications
planning.summary: Anaplan unveiled the Agentic Enterprise, leveraging AI agents to automate finance, supply chain, HR, and sales operations. The company announced agents for the office of the CFO including FP&A, treasury, procurement, controllership, and tax functions, with plans to deliver comprehensive skills-based agents by October 2026.
planning.relevance: Essential for data analytics and AI leaders: Anaplan's shift toward autonomous agents running business operations marks a fundamental re-architecting of enterprise planning workflows, directly addressing the executive mandate to operationalize AI agents at scale.

planning.title: Corporate Functions of the Future: BCG on Agentic Systems, Autonomous Workflows, and AI-Driven Enterprise Operations
planning.summary: BCG describes agentic systems as extending traditional finance functions through continuous orchestrating and execution agents, with humans focusing on judgment, exceptions, and analysis. Organizations can undertake transformation at 0.3% to 1% of annual revenue over 18-36 months with 12-30 month payback periods.
planning.relevance: Strategic for transformation strategy: BCG's Functions of the Future framework models how planning and finance operations will restructure around agentic AI—directly aligned with Anaplan and Pigment product roadmaps.

planning.title: SAP Sapphire 2026: Autonomous Enterprise Announcement, Reltio/Dremio/Prior Labs Acquisitions Shape Agent-Ready Data Architecture
planning.summary: SAP announced the Autonomous Enterprise at Sapphire 2026, acquiring Reltio for master data management, Dremio for Apache Iceberg lakehouse capabilities, and Prior Labs for tabular AI foundation models. The move positions BDC as agent-ready infrastructure with semantic enrichment and federated data access.
planning.relevance: Critical M&A and strategy signal: SAP's three acquisitions reveal the company's deliberate re-architecture of planning and analytics infrastructure around agentic AI—demonstrating competitive moves in response to Pigment and Anaplan market momentum.

planning.title: Finance Transformation Is Necessary: BCG Framework for CFO-Led Modernization of Planning and Decision Infrastructure
planning.summary: BCG outlines five moves for CFO-led finance transformations: pinpointing three targeted changes, recruiting high-influence partners, delivering measurable wins, deploying AI and analytics into live workflows, and sustaining communication. The approach treats technology as incremental investment rather than single transformation bets.
planning.relevance: Directly applicable to data/analytics consulting: BCG's framework emphasizes pragmatic, incremental AI deployment into workflows and decision-making—informing how clients should structure EPM and planning platform adoption programs.

planning.title: SAP Business Data Cloud Consolidates Datasphere, Analytics Cloud, and Curated Content into Unified AI-Ready Platform
planning.summary: SAP's Business Data Cloud (BDC) merges Datasphere, SAP Analytics Cloud, and curated business content into a single governed data platform for enterprise AI. The platform enables zero-copy federation across Snowflake, Databricks, and Microsoft Fabric, with integrations completing through Q3 2026.
planning.relevance: Strategic for enterprise analytics platforms: BDC represents SAP's most significant infrastructure consolidation since S/4HANA, creating a unified data foundation for connected planning and agentic AI—critical context for xP&A modernization strategies.

planning.title: Data Architecture for AI Agents: Gartner Magic Quadrant, xP&A Market Consolidation, and Competitive Landscape 2026
planning.summary: CFO Shortlist's 2026 Anaplan alternatives guide compares enterprise planning vendors including Pigment (Gen-3 FP&A, AI-native, mid-market), OneStream (consolidation leader), Board, Oracle, and SAP. Highlights speed, modern UX, and AI integration as differentiators; consolidation complexity and governance depth as discriminators.
planning.relevance: Essential competitive intelligence: Synthesizes Gartner positioning and CFO evaluation criteria across Pigment, Anaplan, Oracle, SAP, and Board—critical for advising clients on platform selection and competitive dynamics in the fragmented EPM market.

planning.title: Pigment Launches AI Intent Modeling, Approaching $100M ARR with Third Consecutive Year of Doubling
planning.summary: Pigment announced it is approaching $100 million in annual recurring revenue with its ARR doubled for the third consecutive year. The company launched its Modeler Agent, turning weeks-long model-building into hours or minutes through AI intent modeling, with 56% of new customers migrating from legacy vendors in 2025.
planning.relevance: Critical for planning software leaders: Pigment's rapid ARR growth, agentic AI agent maturity, and customer migration patterns from legacy platforms directly inform competitive positioning and market consolidation in modern enterprise planning.

planning.title: Future of FP&A 2026: AI-Driven Forecasting, Continuous Planning, and Finance as Strategic Partner
planning.summary: IBM research shows 69% of CFOs view AI as integral to finance transformation. Deloitte frames FP&A evolution as shifting from reactive analysis to proactive scenario modeling, with AI-powered integration enhancing decision-making across organizational levels. Emphasis on continuous forecasting over annual static budgeting.
planning.relevance: Market validation for planning modernization: IBM and Deloitte research confirms broad CFO commitment to AI-driven FP&A and continuous planning—establishing demand signal for Pigment, Anaplan, and SAP enterprise planning investments.

planning.title: EPM Software Trends 2026: AI-Assisted Planning, xP&A Integration, and Continuous Forecasting Reshape Enterprise Finance
planning.summary: Gartner's December 2025 Magic Quadrant frames financial planning software around FP&A transformation, integrated planning, AI, IBP, and connected data. McKinsey research from November 2025 shows finance teams using AI and agentic AI to forecast accurately, monitor working capital in real time, and surface cost-saving opportunities.
planning.relevance: Foundational for planning leaders: Synthesizes Gartner and McKinsey research on AI adoption in EPM, establishing the category shift from point solutions to integrated, intelligent, continuous planning—the baseline for evaluating Pigment, Anaplan, and SAP positioning.

planning.title: McKinsey on Finance Transformation: Data Governance, Scenario Planning, and CFO Leadership in Enterprise Strategy
planning.summary: McKinsey's Finance 2030 research identifies four imperatives: mastering data, improving decision-making through scenario planning, evolving finance operations, and cultivating finance talent. Emphasizes CFO role in enterprise-wide data governance and scenario-based decision infrastructure.
planning.relevance: Foundational strategy research for planning initiatives: McKinsey's framework on data-driven scenario planning and CFO leadership informs the strategic justification for investing in modern planning and analytics platforms.

research.title: The consulting industry's AI transformation: Toward execution-driven models
research.summary: Industry analysis documenting shift from strategy advisory to AI-enabled delivery and outcome-based pricing. Large firms building governed workflows and embedded execution environments; mid-market generalists face existential pressure; specialists gaining share through narrow high-value expertise.
research.relevance: Critical for understanding how consulting business models are restructuring around AI; reveals how outcome-based pricing, platformization, and specialization are reshaping demand for analytics advisory.

research.title: BCG AI Radar 2026: As AI Investments Surge, CEOs Take the Lead
research.summary: BCG's 2026 global survey of 625 CEOs and board members finds corporations expect to double AI spending from 0.8% to 1.7% of revenues. CEOs spending 8+ hours weekly on AI capabilities are more likely to generate meaningful value; 90%+ plan to maintain or increase AI investments.
research.relevance: Provides C-suite perspective on AI investment prioritization and ROI expectations; indicates structural shifts in how executives are engaging with data & analytics agendas.

research.title: How to Move from AI Experimentation to AI Transformation
research.summary: HBR article from OpenAI and Bain advisors identifies 'micro-productivity trap' where task-level AI gains fail to translate to firm-level value. Successful transformations require organization-wide, outcome-oriented redesigns of processes and value propositions, not isolated tool adoption.
research.relevance: Addresses the organizational coordination challenge that data leaders must solve: moving from siloed AI pilots to integrated, measurable business model transformation.

research.title: Gartner Says Organizations with Successful AI Initiatives Invest Up to Four Times More in Data and Analytics Foundations
research.summary: Gartner survey of 353 D&A and AI leaders finds only 39% confident their AI investments will have positive financial impact. Successful organizations invest 4x more in data quality, governance, AI-ready people, and change management. Through 2030, D&A leader mandate includes trusted data, context foundations, and perceptive intelligence.
research.relevance: Directly targets data & analytics leaders with evidence on investment allocation required for success and governance priorities for enterprise scaling.

research.title: Scaling agentic AI with data transformations
research.summary: McKinsey article identifying that eight in ten companies cite data limitations as a roadblock to scaling agentic AI. Addresses core data architecture, governance, and operating model elements that distinguish companies creating value from AI.
research.relevance: Critical for data leaders planning 2026-2027 infrastructure: directly addresses the data foundation requirements for agentic AI scale and governance-first approaches to enterprise automation.

research.title: AI Will Reshape More Jobs Than It Replaces
research.summary: BCG applies structured microeconomic framework to assess how AI reshapes employment across roles, finding task automation does not equal job loss but substantial role transformation. Software engineers, lawyers, and advisory roles expected to expand rather than contract.
research.relevance: Informs talent strategy and organizational redesign planning for data & analytics leaders; challenges assumptions about AI-driven job displacement in consulting and professional services.

research.title: The $200 Billion Agentic AI Opportunity for Tech Service Providers
research.summary: BCG forecasts agentic AI will drive 0.5-1 percentage point uplift in IT spending as adoption scales, with 40+ percent of large enterprises already scaling agentic implementation. Banking, financial services, and insurance are adoption frontrunners.
research.relevance: Maps enterprise demand for AI-enabled services delivery; essential for understanding consulting business model shifts and where client transformation investments are concentrating.

research.title: M&A Capability for a New Era: Five Ways AI Is Creating More Value in M&A Right Now
research.summary: Bain reports adoption of AI tools in M&A more than doubled in 2025, with 45% of 300+ M&A executives now deploying AI across sourcing, diligence, integration, and learning stages. AI-enabled analytics can reduce deal planning from 12 months to 2 months.
research.relevance: Demonstrates concrete ROI from analytics-driven M&A; shows how AI is reshaping deal economics and accelerating value realization in enterprise transformation contexts.

research.title: The State of AI in the Enterprise - 2026 AI report
research.summary: Deloitte's 2026 report surveying 3,235 global leaders finds worker AI access rose 50% in 2025; companies with 40%+ projects in production expected to double in six months. AI is delivering efficiency/productivity gains, but only 34% are truly reimagining business; skills gap is top barrier.
research.relevance: Broad enterprise perspective on AI adoption maturity; identifies the 'reimagining vs. optimizing' gap and skills shortage as critical bottlenecks for analytics & transformation leaders.

research.title: The state of AI in 2025: Agents, innovation, and transformation
research.summary: McKinsey's 2025 global survey of 1,993 respondents across 105 nations examines how organizations are driving real value from AI, with focus on AI agents, transformation workflows, and the practices that distinguish high performers. Nearly two-thirds of enterprises have experimented with agents, but fewer than 10 percent have scaled them to deliver tangible value.
research.relevance: Provides data & analytics leaders with evidence-based insights on organizational AI maturity, success factors for scaling AI, and the gap between experimentation and enterprise value realization.
